statement: The constructions map a finite binary tree of real pairs to a tree of individual exact or rounded real products; roundedDotProduct then recursively rounds sums along the given tree. The product perturbation theorem bounds each rounded product error by u_M times the absolute exact product. The existence theorem assumes both (depth(T)+1)*u_M<1 and u_M=0 and represents the constructed result as an exact sum of leafwise perturbed products with bound gamma(depth(T)+1,u_M). Under its zero-error hypothesis that bound is zero and the result equals the exact leaf sum of exactProductTree(T). The remaining three targets are defining equations for roundedProductTerm, roundedProductTree, and model multiplication.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation
targets.statement: For every model M and every T in Tree(R x R), put d=depth(T) in the natural numbers and u=u_M in R. If ((d+1) cast to R)*u < 1 and u=0, there exists P in Tree(R) such that IsPerturbation(gamma(d+1,u),exactProductTree(T),P) and exactSum(P)=roundedDotProduct(M,T). Thus P has the same ordered shape as T, and each input leaf (a,b) corresponds to a leaf q of P with |q-a*b| <= gamma(d+1,u)*|a*b|. Its exact leaf sum equals the constructed recursively rounded sum of rounded products. Here gamma(d+1,u)=((d+1)*u)/(1-(d+1)*u). Both hypotheses are explicit. Since u=0, gamma is zero, P equals exactProductTree(T), and round_M is the identity, so the constructed result equals the exact sum of the real leaf products.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTerm.eq_1
targets.statement: For every model M and every x,y in R, roundedProductTerm(M,x,y)=mul_M(x,y). This is the leaf operation used in roundedProductTree, namely round_M(x*y). There are no additional hypotheses beyond M being a model.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree.eq_1
targets.statement: For every model M and every T in Tree(R x R), roundedProductTree(M,T)=map((a,b) -> roundedProductTerm(M,a,b),T). Thus this construction preserves the tree shape and replaces each leaf pair by its rounded product term. There are no additional hypotheses beyond M being a model.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree_isPerturbation
targets.statement: For every model M and every T in Tree(R x R), IsPerturbation(u_M,exactProductTree(T),roundedProductTree(M,T)). The two trees have the same ordered shape; for each input leaf (a,b), their corresponding leaves satisfy |round_M(a*b)-a*b| <= u_M*|a*b|. No depth bound, assumption u_M=0, or assumption u_M<1 is present.

targets.name: Research.FloatingPoint.Model.mul.eq_1
targets.statement: For every model M and every a,b in R, mul_M(a,b)=round_M(a*b), with a*b exact real multiplication. This specifies the operation used by roundedProductTerm, and hence by roundedProductTree and roundedDotProduct. There are no additional hypotheses beyond M being a model.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.exactProductTree
constructions.description: A function Tree(R x R) -> Tree(R) mapping every leaf (a,b) to the real product a*b and preserving all ordered internal nodes. Recursively, exactProductTree(leaf(a,b))=leaf(a*b), and exactProductTree(node(L,R))=node(exactProductTree(L),exactProductTree(R)). It neither multiplies different leaves together nor sums their values.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct
constructions.description: A function Model -> Tree(R x R) -> R defined by roundedDotProduct(M,T)=roundedSum(M,roundedProductTree(M,T)). For S in Tree(R), roundedSum(M,leaf(v))=v and roundedSum(M,node(L,R))=round_M(roundedSum(M,L)+roundedSum(M,R)). Thus each leaf pair first contributes round_M(a*b), and each internal node rounds the sum of its recursively computed child values. A single-leaf input returns round_M(a*b); reading that leaf adds no further rounding. The supplied tree determines the addition order. There is no imposed balancing or vector indexing.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree
constructions.description: A function Model -> Tree(R x R) -> Tree(R) mapping each leaf (a,b) to roundedProductTerm(M,a,b)=mul_M(a,b)=round_M(a*b), preserving the ordered shape. Recursively, roundedProductTree(M,leaf(a,b))=leaf(round_M(a*b)), and roundedProductTree(M,node(L,R))=node(roundedProductTree(M,L),roundedProductTree(M,R)). There is no arithmetic at internal nodes in this construction. This intermediate tree is then reduced by roundedSum in roundedDotProduct.

assumptions: R denotes the real numbers. A model M contains a real u_M with 0<=u_M and a function round_M:R->R such that for every real z there exists a real delta satisfying |delta|<=u_M and round_M(z)=z*(1+delta). These requirements are included whenever a target quantifies over a model. Delta may depend on z; there is no common fixed delta premise.

Model addition and multiplication are add_M(a,b)=round_M(a+b) and mul_M(a,b)=round_M(a*b), for real a,b. No finite representable set, radix, precision, or particular rounding rule is supplied or required.

Tree(A), for an arbitrary label type A, is the inductive type of finite ordered full binary trees, generated by leaf(a) for a in A and node(L,R) for L,R in Tree(A). There is no empty tree constructor. The constructions and input trees in the targets use A=R x R; their product trees and the existential perturbation tree use A=R. No balancing, leaf-count, sign, or nonzero conditions on input leaves are imposed.

For every label type A, depth:Tree(A)->N is defined by depth(leaf(a))=0 and depth(node(L,R))=1+max(depth(L),depth(R)). In the existence target depth(T)+1 is formed in N, then cast to R when multiplied by u_M. map(f,T) applies f to each leaf and preserves every ordered node.
For S in Tree(R), exactSum(leaf(v))=v and exactSum(node(L,R))=exactSum(L)+exactSum(R), using exact real addition.

For a real B and S,P in Tree(R), IsPerturbation(B,S,P) is the inductively generated relation: leaf(x) is related to leaf(y) when |y-x|<=B*|x|; node(L,R) is related to node(Lprime,Rprime) when the corresponding child pairs are related with the same B. Equivalently, S and P have identical ordered shape and satisfy this inequality at every corresponding leaf. The relation itself has no independent premise B>=0.

For every natural k and real u, gamma(k,u)=(k*u)/(1-k*u), with k cast to R. This is defined with real division (which is total in the formal real field, including division by zero). In the existence target k=depth(T)+1 and its explicit strict inequality guarantees a positive denominator. That target also explicitly requires u_M=0; neither hypothesis occurs in the other targets.
